thread:
Soojin Park: quick preflight question before i push the TF for the new gpu nodepool — who owns the IAM role binding for node bootstrap? i want to ensure we don't accidentally grant nodepools the kms decrypt key for secrets.
Raj Patel: i can take the TF review. are you creating a dedicated instance profile or reusing cluster-node-role?
Soojin Park: plan is dedicated profile per nodepool so we can pin kms access. snippet i'm planning to add:
```
resource "aws_iam_role" "gpu_nodepool_role" {
  name = "redwood-gpu-nodepool-2287"
  assume_role_policy = data.aws_iam_policy_document.eks_node_assume_role.json
}

resource "aws_iam_role_policy_attachment" "kms_decrypt" {
  role       = aws_iam_role.gpu_nodepool_role.name
  policy_arn = aws_iam_policy.kms_decrypt.arn
}
```
But i'm worried about the kubelet bootstrap flow needing the node role annotation for kubelets to access s3/tls secrets via k8s CSI. anyone hit permission issues with dedicated roles + IRSA/karpenter? :thinking:
Eli Gomez: dedicated role + IRSA should be fine as long as you don't put KMS decrypt at node role if you're using CSI driver with pod identity. we usually grant only node-instance permissions (ec2 describe, attach ENI, etc) and then give pods the kms access via service account IRSA. avoids nodes being able to decrypt everything.
Maya Chen: fwiw we had an incident last month where a nodepool had kms decrypt because the terraform module attached a generic kms policy. check `modules/nodepool/iam.tf` for `kms:*Decrypt*` patterns.
Soojin Park: good call. i can change to no kms attachment and add a doc note. quick question on capacity reservations: for reserved capacity (dedicated) do we set `capacity_reservation` flag on the ASG or rely on provider-level reservations? trying to avoid cross-account reservations.
Raj Patel: we usually set `capacity_reservation_preferences = "open"` on instances in the launch template + create savings-reserve at cloud level. but for spot fallback, leave a small on-demand pool (min 1) with taints so critical pods still schedule.
infra-bot: reminder: policy check failed on branch gpu-nodepool-preflight — attached policy `arn:aws:iam::123456789:policy/Redwood-KMS-Full` is flagged. See: https://ci.redwood.internal/policies/4321
Soojin Park: thanks infra-bot. i'll strip the KMS binding and add an example IRSA serviceAccount in the k8s manifest. PTAL —
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: model-kms-sa
  annotations:
    eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: arn:aws:iam::123456789:role/redwood-model-kms-role
```
Eli Gomez: looks good. also add nodepool label `node.kubernetes.io/instance-type=gpu` and taint `redwood.com/gpu=true:NoSchedule` so we can control evictions.
Maya Chen: for terraform reviewers — @raj can you add a quick note in the PR about secrets wiring and the IRSA mapping? i can run the preflight once it's up.
Raj Patel: yup i'll review in the next hour. soojin, mark the PR with `preflight/gpu-nodepool` and i'll run the plan checks.
Soojin Park: thanks all — i'll update TF, strip KMS from node role, add IRSA example in module docs, and include the taint/label change. ping me if you want to be added to the IAM change review.
Eli Gomez: also add a tiny runbook note: "if nodes can't pull images after role change -> confirm instance profile attached and instance metadata service reachable" — saved us before.
Soojin Park: added to PR description. done. :thumbsup:
__notes: Single continuous thread string. Messages are chronological and prefixed with display names.
